utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4, paragraph 12 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, sir, we're still trying to get there. Four.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've got the, by the look of it, the end page which is signed by Ambassador Donnelly, if that's the one you are -

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's the one I'm looking at, and I am looking paragraph where you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is the paragraph that the witness already said he wouldn't comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He wasn't asked about that one section. I don't know if he was referring to just the items that Mr. Ackerman had pointed out to him or the suggestion there that, as it says here. I don't want to misquote it. "He may have an eye to possible ICTY investigations recent events, and was very keen to shuffle responsibility to the MUP." I believe that was not one that had been raised by Mr. Ackerman, and that is why I wanted to ask this witness whether he had the same position with respect to that statement or whether he did have some light to shed on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think with respect to the Court, it would be inappropriate for me to comment on what the ambassador has stated. I have given you my comments on General Dimitrijevic and General Perisic and even General Kirby's suggestions at time that they disagreed with what was going on. And I hope I have explained why I reported it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is fair enough, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can move on then. Would you agree with me that all the matters that are contained in your statement and your testimony here these -- these last two days has been limited to the time period before March 23rd, 1999, and after the conclusion of the NATO bombing campaign, that is to say that you cannot offer us with a degree of certainty concrete testimony relating to the time period between 23rd March, 1999, and the return of KFOR to Kosovo after the conclusion of the NATO bombings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I -- I was not physically in Kosovo for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was working back in the Ministry of Defence advising my -- my defence about the Yugoslav position, and as I've said again, playing the Yugoslav card in a rather depressing situation, to be quite blunt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. I've got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you find a suitable place to end --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was going to suggest-- I have two short questions and then I'll moving to another topic, so I'll try and get through the two questions and we can interrupt if that's okay with Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, a state of war was declared by Yugoslavia on the 25th of March, 1999, as a result of the NATO bombings. Am I will correct that you do not have any specific knowledge from any source as to what effect this decision had upon how the MUP of the Republic of Serbia was organised or functioned under such circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I repeat, sir, I was -- I was then back in London and one was then reacting and briefing to the situation as it unfurled during those days. So I really can't comment on the state of war. It's -- I don't think the UK has declared a state of war for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could probably pause now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we have to finish there for today, and you will have to return tomorrow. We only have Mr. Ivetic's cross-examination to complete and then re-examination by the Prosecution. I understand you're intending to leave tomorrow. Do you have a time for leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With respect, I have got an important engagement tomorrow night at about half past 6.00, about two on a half hours west of London, so I need to leave here by mid-morning in order to catch the plane and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll be sitting at 9.00, and everyone, I think, has that target clearly in mind. So your evidence should be completed in good time for you to make your travel arrangements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Meanwhile, please remember to discuss anything but the evidence with anyone you meet tonight, and we'll see you again tomorrow at 9.00. We'll go into closed session while you leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 8th day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.29 p.m.,
